author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Rhode Island health and environmental officials lifted their recommendation to avoid recreational activity at Georgiaville Pond in Smithfield after testing indicated that the harmful algae bloom there had cleared.

The Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management and the state Department of Health said Monday that the Georgiaville advisory could be removed. The update follows water sampling and laboratory testing conducted as officials monitored conditions at the pond.

The agencies continued to recommend avoiding all contact with Lower Melville Pond in Portsmouth, where recreational activity remains a high risk. The warning applies to people and pets and includes swimming, wading and other direct contact with the water.

Officials also advise against drinking water from the affected pond or eating fish taken from it. People who experience symptoms after possible exposure should seek medical advice. The agencies said conditions can change, so residents should check state advisories before returning to recreational waters.
dek: State health and environmental officials lifted a recreational warning for Georgiaville Pond in Smithfield while keeping a high-risk contact advisory in place for Lower Melville Pond.
headline: Rhode Island lifts Georgiaville Pond algae advisory after bloom clears
sourceName: Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management
